explanation: Archive-only notes. Observed baseline: 8 tasks failed with error_kind=object_type at first_invalid_action=0 (plan length 8-11), and 2 tasks failed with sandbox_execution_failed / resource_limit. Hypotheses: (a) the grounding heuristic in the previous revision misclassified objects (its "at" heuristic added both spanners and nuts to the same set and it never restricted action arguments to properly declared types), which can yield a first action whose objects are of the wrong declared type; (b) exhaustive BFS over the full state space can blow up on the larger instances, matching the resource_limit outcomes. Repair: bind every action argument strictly from declared object types (man/location/spanner/nut), and replace BFS with a bounded constructive planner (walk along shortest link path, pick up a co-located useable spanner, tighten one nut at a time), which is O(nuts * men * spanners) with small constants and never explores a state space. Domain definition, output format, action argument order, step cap of 1000, stdlib-only and no-mutation rules are preserved. Alternative explanations cannot be excluded from the recorded evidence, and a fix for these two recorded failure modes does not establish success on any unseen instance; no optimality or generality claim is made.
